chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub, from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from Ibn Abi 'Umayr, from Hammad, from al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

Her khul' (redemption/divorce initiated by wife) is not valid until she says to her husband: 'By Allah, I will not fulfill your oath, nor obey your command, nor perform ghusl for you from janabah, and I will surely bed your bed, and I will surely give adhan (call to prayer) upon you without your permission.' The people used to grant permission (for khul') for less than this. So when the woman says that to her husband, what he took from her becomes lawful for him, and she remains with him having two remaining divorces. And the khul' was considered one divorce. And he said: The speech must come from her (not the husband). And he said: If the matter were up to us, we would not validate a divorce except for the waiting period (i.e., khul' counts as one irrevocable divorce, not three).

key_terms.لِلْعِدَّةِ: For the waiting period (referring to the nature of the divorce)

ai.seo_question: What are the specific verbal conditions required for a valid khul' divorce in Shia fiqh?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfahani’s al-Istibsar establishes the rigorous evidentiary standard for *khul'*, requiring the wife to explicitly renounce her marital rights (*nushuz*) through specific declarations of disobedience, thereby transforming the transaction into a binding revocable divorce. It highlights the juristic nuance that while *khul'* is treated as one of the three divorces, the Imams preferred it to be counted as a final divorce (*mubarrqa*) to prevent indefinite marital limbo, reflecting the principle of *takhayyur* (choice) in marital dissolution.
